newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks rally to close at session.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks rally to close at session.

text.p: Argentine stocks powered ahead in heavy turnover Thursday and were expected to end the weak on a firm note, dealers said.

"The market looks healthy and should keep growing if U.S. long bond yields manage to stabilize at current levels," said Roberto Agra of brokers Agra y Cia. "But investors have turned much more cautious in the past few days -- for the time being we won't see any bold positioning."
The blue-chip MerVal index advanced 1.8 percent to close at session highs of 689.21, stretching its three-day rally to five percent.
Traders said bolsa players expected the U.S. Federal Reserve to leave interest rates unchanged when it meets next Tuesday and Wednesday.
"All the latest indicators seem to point in that direction, which is why Wall Street is rebounding and the Latin American markets have fallen back in favor with foreign investors," said Agra.
Analysts said the government's $500 million, 10-year Eurobond placement Wednesday helped sentiment recover on the bolsa after a sharp four-day slide which was snapped last Tuesday.

"The overall picture is good -- economic fundamentals are steadily improving and financing plans for this year's heavy debt payments have been unfolding smoothly," another trader said. She was referring to Argentina's successful launch last week of a $2.0 billion, 20-year global bond.
Floor volume recovered to 30.2 million pesos in the session from 18.3 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter turnover soared to 159.9 million pesos from Wednesday's dismal tally of 35.7 million.
The bolsa's all-share index closed up 2.5 percent, with winners smashing losers 35 to 13 and 14 stocks closing flat.

Best main-tier performers were Banco Francs, Telefnica and real estate developer Irsa, which rocketed 6.7 percent, 5.4 percent and 4.3 percent, respectively. Banco de Galicia rose 3.7 percent and Telecom 3.4 percent.
The only MerVal losers were oil company Astra and power utility Central Puerto, both off 0.7 percent.
